    AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                               §

                        Request for Corrections to
                      SOAH Order No. 30, Attachment B

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
         Save Our Salado (SOS) respectfully requests that SOAH Order No. 30,
Attachment B, be corrected to list each intervenor whom the Administrative Law Judges
already admitted as a party under the “Save Our Salado” entry in SOAH Order No. 14,
but whose name was omitted from Attachment B. The relief requested is ministerial:
it asks only that Attachment B be conformed to the admitting order the ALJs entered.

                                           I. The Request

        Attachment B lists intervenors by the first link that affects them, assigns a party or
intervenor number, identifies each intervenor’s representation, and lists all links affecting
that party. On April 27, 2026, over sixty individuals filed a Joint Request to Intervene,
each identified by name and address in Attachment A to that request. 1 Each individual
appointed Save Our Salado (SOS) as their authorized representative and designated Nikki
Segal as the contact for service in this docket; SOS did not itself seek party status.




1
    Joint Request to Intervene (Apr. 27, 2026) (Interchange Item No. 3139).
         In SOAH Order No. 14, the Administrative Law Judges granted those requests
and admitted each individual as a party, listing every one of them by name under the
single entry “Save Our Salado, comprising” the named members. 2
        SOS also filed a Joint Position Statement opposing Link E12, and each member
who appointed SOS as authorized representative is identified on Attachment A to that
Joint Position Statement. 3 SOS therefore requests that Attachment B to SOAH Order No.
30 be updated to include each individual identified in the Joint Request to Intervene and
the Joint Position Statement.
        Each individual on Attachment A to the Joint Request to Intervene should appear
as an intervenor on Attachment B. SOS is not a law firm and represents no intervenor as a
lawyer; as the members’ authorized representative, however, SOS may properly be listed
in the “Represented By” column for each of them on Attachment B to SOAH Order No.
30.
        The requested format is already the ALJs’ own convention. In SOAH Order No.
14, the Administrative Law Judges rendered comparable representative groups by listing
each member individually — for example, “Save the Lampasas, comprising …” and
“M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners, comprising …” — as they did for the
Save Our Salado entry. Attachment B can list the individual SOS intervenors for Party
Number 204 in the same way, consistent with how it already lists Save the Lampasas 25,
Inc. (Party Number 392) and Lampasas J11 Landowners (Party Number 503).
       Party status matters to each intervenor. They organized and coordinated with their
neighbors to intervene, several filed direct testimony, and all joined the Joint Position
Statement opposing Link E12. Because Order No. 14 already admitted them as parties,


2
  SOAH Order No. 14, Granting Motions to Intervene, at 25 (May 15, 2026) (Interchange Item No. 4679)
(“Save Our Salado, comprising Stephanie D. and Mark Allen; Kathleen D'Ann Bartek; Melanie Billek;
Kyle Little; Stephen Cox; Jason and Meredith Bonnett; Elizabeth Bullock; Daryl and April Ciano; Brian
Cornett; Cecil and Virginia Capps Cospor; Brandon and Raven Crook; Jared and Lacey Cruddas; Terry
D. and Suzanne M. Culp; Megan and Jennifer McDonald David; Megan and Jennifer McDonald David;
Johnny and Melissa (Stewart) Davidson; Daniel and Stephanie Delgado; Nichole and Calvin Dockray;
Caron L. Drake; Steven Earman and Lisa Spence; Craig and Carleen Edwards; Tommy G. and Sandra
Emmons; McKayla Falcone; Alexandris and Daniel Ferenczy; Steve and Kaitlin Fox; Luke and Jacquiline
Franks; Andrew and Kim Frascone; Glenda Kay Hill; Brenda K. and Jim Holder; David R. Holyfield and
Paula Lalande; Nathan Ray and Kristin Houston; Gretchen Jahna; Dusty Jahna Ramsey; Ricky and Ann
Lindsey; Samantha Loth and Andrew Markley; Stephen R. and Susan E. Miller; Larry (Bear) and Kate
MISSTEX aka Rosamond; Gunter, Matthew, Laci MLOA Family Trust; Charles R. and Gay Nell Morison;
Timothy A, Netters, Jr.; Erin and Zach Oldham; Charles and Caitlyn Ormond; Lois L. Parish; Erin and
Timothy Petty; Jesse and Sally Rhymes; Howard Robert Sartor; Jeffrey and Nicole L. Segal; Brian and
Shannon Seib; Kelly T. and Jessica Sharpe; Dalyn R. and Alexander Smith; Martin and Karen Spettel;
Bree Carrico Stagecoach Inn; Melissa A. Stewart; Anthony Michael and Kendal Lee Taylor; Aaron and
Andrea Taylor; Robb and Sara Wilgoren; Mary Woodlief; Stephen Zahirniak and Rhonda Anderson; and
Randy and Rita Zbranek”).
3
  Joint Position Statement (May 13, 2026) (Interchange Item No. 4389).


         Save Our Salado (SOS); Request for Corrections to SOAH Order No. 30, Attachment B
 listing their names on Attachment B is necessary so the official party record accurately
reflects the ALJs’ ruling.

                                    II. Conclusion

       For these reasons, the Save Our Salado intervenors respectfully request that the
Administrative Law Judges correct Attachment B to SOAH Order No. 30 to list each
individual identiﬁed in Attachment A — each of whom was admitted as a party in SOAH
Order No. 14 — and grant such other relief as may be just.

                                        Respectfully submitted,

                                        Bayliff Law Firm PLLC
                                        420 Crosswind Drive
                                        Blanco, Texas 78606

                                        By:

                                        Bradford W. Bayliff
                                        State Bar No. 24012260
                                        (512) 225-0027
                                        Brad@Bayliff.Law

                                        Administrative Assistance for
                                        Save Our Salado (SOS)

                                 Certificate of Service
       A copy of this document is being filed in the Public Utility Commission’s
Interchange system and served on all parties of record as required by the orders in this
docket, the Commission’s rules, and the Commission’s First and Second Orders
Suspending Rules issued on March 16, 2020 and July 16, 2020 in Project No. 50664.
                                                        /s/ Bradford W. Bayliff
